task: packets/INDEX.json declares "schema": "genesis.packet-index.v1", but unlike genesis.packet.v1 and genesis.receipt.v1 (both of which have a real JSON Schema file under their own schemas/ directory), no genesis.packet-index.v1.schema.json exists anywhere in this repository - tools/validate_packet.py's check_index() validates the index's on-disk consistency (hashes, statuses, orphans) but never checks the index file's own top-level shape against a written-down schema. Write packets/schemas/genesis.packet-index.v1.schema.json (draft 2020-12, in the same style as the two existing schema files: $id, title, description, additionalProperties: false, required, $defs as needed) describing the actual shape already in use: {schema: const genesis.packet-index.v1, description: string, updatedAt: date-time, packets: array of {id, status, path, sha256} with sha256 constrained to 64 lowercase hex chars}. Then make tools/validate_packet.py's check_index() load and enforce that schema on the index's top-level object before doing its existing on-disk cross-checks, so a malformed index (wrong types, missing updatedAt, an extra unknown key) fails with a schema error instead of a confusing downstream KeyError or silent pass. Add tests in tests/test_validate_packet.py for: a well-formed index passing the new schema check, and at least two malformed-index cases (missing required key; wrong type for packets) each producing a clear schema-shape error rather than a crash.
doneCriteria: packets/schemas/genesis.packet-index.v1.schema.json exists and matches the index shape genesis-web actually uses (checked against the real packets/INDEX.json in this repo, which must still validate)
